04Using the ToolsUSING▶
  • No accountOpen the link and use the tool. There is nothing to install and no sign-in.
  • In your browserEach tool is a single web page that does its work on your own computer.
  • BrowsersUse a current Chrome, Edge, Safari, or Firefox on a desktop or laptop. The 3D views need a computer with graphics support, which almost every recent one has.
  • Saving filesExports save straight to your browser's Downloads folder. Large meshes come zipped.
  • Blank viewerIf a 3D view stays blank, close other heavy tabs and reload, or try another browser.
Bookmark itEach tool keeps the same link forever, so a bookmark always opens the newest version.
05Updates & Versions (explained)UPDATES▶
  • Same linksTool links never change. When a tool is updated, the same link opens the new version; reload the page if it still looks old.
  • Version dateEach tool shows its version date in its header, matching the Updated column in Tool Library (open from here).
  • Where they liveThe tools are kept on GitHub, which records every version: vibe-tools on GitHub ↗
  • SkillsWant Claude to build pages like these? See Swami's Claude Skills ↗.
  • ProblemsUse the Swami link at the bottom of this page to email what happened, which tool, and which browser.

07GlossaryREFERENCE▶

Every term with a dotted underline in the dashboard links here — hover it for a quick definition, click it to land on its row. In the Appears in column, each number is a jump link to where that term is used in that section; the term flashes green when you arrive. Qty counts every mention across the content sections. Each term's Topic tag names what it is about, one color per topic.

TermTopicDefinitionAppears inQty
GitHubLibraryWebsite that hosts the tools and keeps a record of every version.
Version dateLibraryThe date a tool was last changed, shown in its header and in the Updated column.
BrowserUsingThe program you view web pages with, such as Chrome, Edge, Safari, or Firefox.
ExportUsingSaving a file a tool made, such as a mesh or an image, to your computer.
Mesh3DA 3D shape made of many small flat faces, saved as STL or OBJ.
Relief3DA carving that rises from a flat background, like a sign or a coin.
Height map3DA grayscale image where brighter means higher and darker means lower.
STL3DThe most common 3D mesh file type, read by slicers and CAM software.
OBJ3DA 3D mesh file type that can keep four-sided faces and textures.
CNCMakingComputer-controlled cutting machines, such as a wood router.
ToolpathMakingThe path a CNC cutter follows to carve a shape.
ZipUsingA compressed file that holds one or more files; open it to get them out.
ClaudeLibraryAnthropic's AI assistant, which Swami vibe codes these tools with.
